evidence.requirements: Most of the brief is met. The list page has the heading, 25 links whose text equals `name`, family, L3, Search, Family select and an aria-live count (app.js:32-62, list.jpg). Search ignores the comma/point difference, so `7,62 x 51` finds 308 Win. (format.js:135-144). Detail views use hash routes (app.js:152-165) and show the full metadata, the capacity link, Symbol/Value/Unit tables grouped by section, Print and All cartridges. The SVG is true to scale with aria-label `<name> drawing` (drawing.js:248). It has a title block with name, table, revised date, 'Dimensions in mm' and a 10 mm scale bar. Print fits one A4 page with a footer (print-308_win.jpg). No dependencies; the data is embedded so the app works from file://. Partly met: (a) 'labels legible / no overlap': on short cases the L3 label is wider than its dimension line, and its knock-out rectangle hides the line, the arrowheads and the extension lines (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). (b) 'cut walls hatched': the hatch pitch is 1.5 mm and the walls are about 0.6 mm (drawing.js:249), so the walls look almost unhatched. (c) The α dimension spans the half-angle to the axis, not the included angle (drawing.js:142-155, plan.md decision 8). (d) Heeled 22 LR has no visible mouth face in the outside view (rule 6).
evidence.correctness: I checked the geometry against rules 1-8 and it follows them closely. Chamfer `min(f·tanβ, R1/4)` (geometry.js:208-210). Groove floor and ramp (219-241). Belt ramp at δ to R3/2, then to E, then a step to P1/2; for 300 WM this gives rampEnd 3.24 < E 5.59 (230-233). Rimfire half-round with its apex at R1/2 (195-204). Shoulder fillets r1 min and r2 (88-105). Tangent ogive with the correct ρ and an endpoint check (142-150). Quarter-ellipse and cone noses, and the s/k/m tables per category (116-131). Heeled diameter H2 and heel H2−2tb (110-111, 325). Walls tb/tn blended across the shoulder (279-291). w as the max of the listed terms (300-303) and pocket sizes by primer type (12-20). Scale checks in the screenshots: 308 L3 is about 429 px and R1 about 100 px, both near 8.3 px/mm, so proportions are true. Outlines match reference/308_win.png, 300_win_mag.png and 9_mm_luger.png. Labels match the data, tolerances included: `L1 39.62 -0.2`, `R 1.4 -0.25`, `α 10°58'00"` (detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). Defects: the α arc shows α/2 but carries α. Diameter extension lines start 0.6 mm past the feature and run horizontally to beyond the tip, so the P1/P2 lines lie almost on the body outline and the outline looks doubled (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-300_win_mag.jpg, detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). The 9 mm L3 label hides its own dimension line. The print view fits one A4 page.
evidence.security: The DOM is built with createElement and textContent (app.js:10-23). The only innerHTML is the SVG string (app.js:113), and its name and label text go through escapeXml (drawing.js:35-39, 244, 270). The pattern id interpolates record.key without escaping (drawing.js:245). No eval or Function in the app (vm is used only in tests/helpers.js). No fetch, CDN or font requests. External capacity links use rel=noopener.
evidence.code_quality: There are four small modules with a clear split: format, geometry, drawing, app. They use UMD-style exports so the same files are tested in Node. Names are clear and constants are named. The drawing is wrapped in try/catch with a user-facing error, and notes record missing values. Weak points: profile() is about 200 lines (geometry.js:163-364). The CSS class `.values` is used both for the column wrapper and for the tables, so column-width also applies to table.values (styles.css:321, 338). The returned `values` object is built with repetitive ternaries (geometry.js:343-345).
evidence.tests: About 35 node:test cases. geometry.test.js checks rim type, chamfer, groove order, belt ramp, rimfire apex, s/k/m and meplat for each nose, heeled heel radius, tn/tb, w and pocket sizes, and missing-value notes. format.test.js checks symbols, units, angles, tolerance merging, that every field of all 25 records appears exactly once, and search. drawing.test.js checks the required labels for all records and runs an overlap check for all 25. Gaps: the overlap oracle ignores dimension lines, arrows and extension lines, so it passes while the 9 mm and 22 LR L3 labels visibly cover their arrows. Ogive radius, fillets, the shoulder wall blend and the α arc are not tested. No DOM or routing, file://, network, or print-one-page tests are committed; plan.md:13 calls them scratch. plan.md:64 lists tests/data.test.js, which does not exist.
evidence.ux_design: The pages are dense and calm for a technical audience: two-column metadata and three-column right-aligned tabular tables (detail-308_win.jpg). The print layout uses four compact columns on one page. The drawing is weaker. On rifle pages the case covers only about 60% of the content width. Six diameter columns past the tip create a band of near-parallel grey extension lines, and the tiny α arc is hard to read. On pistols and rimfire the fixed 66 mm title block is wider than the cartridge, so labels become about 35 px tall and dominate the view (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). The notes ('Rim: rimless', 'Bullet nose: pointy') are useful. Dark mode exists in CSS (styles.css:16-26) but there is no screenshot of it.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img and aria-label `<name> drawing`. Tables have th scope=col and scope=row (app.js:66, 76). The search and select have real labels (app.js:28-30). The count is aria-live polite and there is a visible :focus-visible outline (styles.css:55-58). Controls are at least 44 px high, html has lang=en, and muted text contrast is about 6:1. Missing: no focus move or heading focus on hash navigation, no skip link, and tables have no caption (the section h3 is outside the table). The drawing's alt text is only its name, though every value is also in the tables.
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML/CSS/JS, no runtime or dev dependencies (package.json has only the test script). The source is about 900 lines for a parametric drawing engine plus the UI, which fits the problem. There are no needless abstractions.
evidence.maintainability: The README explains how to run and test the app and maps each file (README.md). The spec, plan (with 12 recorded decisions) and tasks are in specs/001-cartridge-reference/. Regression unit tests exist. Missing: no CI configuration, no Node version pin (no engines field or .nvmrc), no changelog or release process beyond version 1.0.0, and no ADRs. The browser and print checks were run from an uncommitted scratch playwright install. The docs contradict each other: plan.md:57 says 'two-column table layout' while CSS uses four columns (styles.css:511), and plan.md:64 lists a test file that does not exist.
evidence.visual_design: The type is restrained system sans with tabular numbers, uppercase small section heads, muted labels and consistent rules between pages (list.jpg, detail-*.jpg). It looks finished. The drawing's line weights are reasonable and the knock-out labels read cleanly on rifle cases. Two things are inconsistent: label and title block size varies a lot between cartridges because the fixed title block sets the viewBox, and the grey extension-line bundles look unfinished next to the clean reference drawings.
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is clear: back link and Print, then name, metadata, drawing, notes and tables (detail-308_win.jpg). The page does not overflow, and print fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). Problems: on short cases the title block outweighs the part and pushes the tables down (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). Labels cover dimension lines and arrowheads. On the list page the name is far left and the family and L3 are far right, a long scan across 1100 px (list.jpg).
evidence.usability: Tasks take few steps. Search filters live, the family filter works, the count updates, and each name opens a bookmarkable detail view. 'All cartridges' and the header link go back, Print uses the native dialog, and unknown keys show a not-found page with a link back (app.js:143-150). The search text and filter are lost when returning to the list, because renderList rebuilds the inputs on every hashchange (app.js:34-38).
evidence.reception: Reloaders and gunsmiths would trust the complete, correctly formatted C.I.P. values and the true-to-scale drawings, and would likely reuse it as a quick reference and print sheet. Engineers would notice the α arc marking the half-angle, the doubled outlines from the extension lines, and the oversized labels and title block on pistol drawings. These cost some professional credibility.

unmet_requirements: Labels on short cases are not fully legible: the L3 label is wider than its dimension line and its knock-out box hides the line, arrowheads and extension lines (9 mm Luger, 22 Long Rifle)
Cut walls are barely hatched: the 1.5 mm hatch pitch is wider than the ~0.6 mm walls
The shoulder angle dimension draws the half-angle to the axis but is labelled with the included angle α
Heeled case (22 Long Rifle): the mouth face is not visible in the outside view (rule 6)
strengths: The geometry engine follows the brief's rules faithfully: chamfer, groove, belt at δ, rimfire half-round, shoulder fillets, tangent ogive, nose and seating tables, heeled bullet, walls, w and primer pocket. Drawings are true to scale and match the reference outlines.

Data is shown completely and as specified: every field appears exactly once, tolerances sit next to their values and appear in the drawing labels, angles read like 39°59'49", units are correct, and the tables are grouped by section.
No dependencies; works from file:// with hash routes; a clean one-page A4 black-on-white print with a source footer.
issues: Dimension drafting defects: diameter extension lines run full length almost on top of the body outline and make it look doubled (308 Win., 300 Win. Mag., 44 Rem. Mag.), and on short cases the L3 label hides its own dimension line and arrowheads (9 mm Luger, 22 Long Rifle). The overlap test cannot catch either because it ignores dimension and extension lines.
Drawing semantics and scale: the α arc spans α/2 but is labelled α; wall hatching is barely visible; the fixed 66 mm title block dominates pistol and rimfire drawings and blows up their labels.
Maintainability and test gaps: no CI, no Node version pin, no committed browser, routing or print tests, and the plan contradicts the code (missing data.test.js; 'two-column' vs four-column print).
review.verdict: This is a careful, dependency-free reference app: its geometry follows the brief's rules closely, its data tables are complete and correct, and its print view fits one page. It still needs another pass on dimension drafting (extension-line clutter, labels covering arrows on short cases, the half-angle α arc) and on CI and browser tests before it goes to an engineering audience.
